name: 100ms
description: Reads 100ms rooms, sessions, recordings, templates, live streams, external streams, recording assets, and webhook events, and writes room/template/room-code/recording lifecycle mutations, through the 100ms server-side REST API.

management_token.description: 100ms management token. Used only for Bearer auth; never logged.

base_url.description: 100ms API base URL override for tests or proxies.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

write_actions.name: create_room
write_actions.risk: creates a new 100ms room, or upserts an existing room's template if the same name is reused (100ms's own documented create-with-existing-name behavior); external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: update_room
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing room's metadata, or disables/re-enables it via the enabled field (100ms's disable/enable API is the same POST /rooms/{id} endpoint); disabling blocks all future joins to that room. External mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: create_template
write_actions.risk: creates a new room-policy template (roles/settings); external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: create_room_code
write_actions.risk: generates join-authentication room codes for every role in the named room; codes act as join credentials, external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: update_room_code
write_actions.risk: enables or disables a specific join-credential room code; disabling revokes that code's ability to join. External mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: start_recording
write_actions.risk: starts a composite recording job for the named room; consumes recording/storage quota. External mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: stop_recording
write_actions.risk: stops all recording jobs currently running in the named room; external mutation, approval required

risk.read: external 100ms API read of rooms, sessions, recordings, templates, live streams, external streams, recording assets, and webhook events
risk.write: external 100ms mutation: creates/updates rooms, creates templates, creates/updates room join-codes, and starts/stops room recordings; approval required

description: Reads Acuity Scheduling appointments, clients, appointment types, calendars, forms, products, orders, and labels, and writes appointment/block/certificate mutations, through the Acuity REST API.

username.description: Acuity account User ID, sent as the HTTP Basic auth username.

base_url.description: Acuity API base URL override for tests or proxies.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

write_actions.name: create_appointment
write_actions.risk: creates a live appointment booking on the calendar and, depending on account settings, sends the client a confirmation email/SMS; external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: update_appointment
write_actions.risk: updates a live appointment's client-facing details from Acuity's white-list of updatable attributes; external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: cancel_appointment
write_actions.risk: permanently cancels a live scheduled appointment; irreversible (Acuity's own docs: it is not possible to un-cancel), and by default sends the client a cancellation notification. External mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: create_block
write_actions.risk: blocks off a time range on a live calendar, preventing clients from booking appointments in it; external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: create_certificate
write_actions.risk: issues a live, redeemable package or coupon certificate code; external mutation, approval required

risk.read: external Acuity Scheduling API read of appointments, clients, appointment types, calendars, forms, products, orders, and labels
risk.write: external Acuity Scheduling mutation: creates/updates/cancels live appointments, blocks off calendar time, and issues package/coupon certificates; approval required

name: aircall
description: Reads Aircall calls, users, contacts, numbers, teams, tags, and webhooks, and writes user/team/contact/tag/webhook mutations plus call archive/comment/tag actions, through the Aircall REST API.

api_id.description: Aircall API ID, used as the HTTP Basic auth username. Never logged.

api_token.description: Aircall API token, used as the HTTP Basic auth password. Never logged.

base_url.description: Aircall API base URL override for tests or proxies.

start_date.description: RFC3339 lower bound; only calls/contacts created at or after this time are read (sent as the unix-seconds `from` filter).

write_actions.name: create_user
write_actions.risk: creates a new Aircall agent seat, which may consume a billable license; external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: update_user
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing agent's profile/availability; a visible change for that agent's call routing

write_actions.name: delete_user
write_actions.risk: permanently removes an Aircall agent seat; irreversible, frees the associated license; approval required

write_actions.name: create_team
write_actions.risk: creates a new team container; low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: delete_team
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a team; agents assigned to it lose that team's routing/membership immediately

write_actions.name: add_user_to_team
write_actions.risk: adds an agent to a team, changing that agent's call routing/membership; low-risk, reversible via remove_user_from_team

write_actions.name: remove_user_from_team
write_actions.risk: removes an agent from a team, changing that agent's call routing/membership immediately

write_actions.name: create_contact
write_actions.risk: creates a new shared/personal directory contact; low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_contact
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing contact's directory record, including its full phone_numbers/emails arrays (a partial array here replaces the previous set)

write_actions.name: delete_contact
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a directory contact; irreversible

write_actions.name: create_tag
write_actions.risk: creates a new call-tagging label; low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_tag
write_actions.risk: renames or recolors an existing tag; a visible change everywhere the tag is already applied

write_actions.name: delete_tag
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a tag; it is un-applied from every call that previously carried it

write_actions.name: create_webhook
write_actions.risk: registers a new outbound webhook that will POST live call/event data to an external URL of the caller's choosing; verify the target endpoint before enabling

write_actions.name: update_webhook
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing webhook's target URL, subscribed events, or active state; a changed url redirects future event deliveries to a different endpoint

write_actions.name: delete_webhook
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a webhook subscription; event delivery to its target URL stops immediately

write_actions.name: archive_call
write_actions.risk: marks a call as archived, hiding it from default call-list views; reversible via unarchive_call

write_actions.name: unarchive_call
write_actions.risk: restores a previously archived call to default call-list views

write_actions.name: comment_call
write_actions.risk: adds an internal comment note to a call record; visible to other agents with call access, no external side effect

write_actions.name: tag_call
write_actions.risk: applies the given tags to a call; additive, does not remove tags already present

risk.read: external Aircall API read of call, contact, and directory data
risk.write: external Aircall API mutation of agents, teams, contacts, tags, webhooks, and call archive/comment/tag state; approval required for user/team/contact/webhook create-update-delete, low-risk for additive call tagging/commenting

name: airtable
description: Reads Airtable bases, tables, records, webhooks, and record comments, and writes record/table/field/comment/webhook mutations, through the Airtable Web API.

api_key.description: Airtable Personal Access Token, sent as a Bearer token. Preferred over access_token when both are set. Never logged.

access_token.description: Airtable OAuth2 access token, sent as a Bearer token when api_key is unset. Never logged.

base_url.description: Airtable API base URL override for tests or proxies.

base_id.description: Airtable base id (required for the 'tables' and 'records' streams).

table_id.description: Airtable table id or name (required for the 'records' stream).

page_size.description: Records per page for the 'records' stream (1-100).

write_actions.name: create_record
write_actions.risk: creates a new record in the configured base/table; low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_record
write_actions.risk: mutates only the field values included in the request (non-destructive PATCH); unincluded cell values are left unchanged

write_actions.name: delete_record
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a record from the base/table; irreversible

write_actions.name: create_table
write_actions.risk: creates a new table (schema mutation) in the configured base; low-risk but changes the base's structure, visible to every collaborator

write_actions.name: update_table
write_actions.risk: renames or redescribes an existing table; a visible schema change for every collaborator on the base

write_actions.name: create_field
write_actions.risk: creates a new column (schema mutation) in the target table; low-risk but changes the table's structure, visible to every collaborator

write_actions.name: update_field
write_actions.risk: renames or redescribes an existing column; a visible schema change for every collaborator on the base

write_actions.name: create_comment
write_actions.risk: adds a visible comment to a record; every base collaborator with record access can see it, no external side effect

write_actions.name: update_comment
write_actions.risk: edits the text of an existing comment; visible to every base collaborator with record access

write_actions.name: delete_comment
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a comment from a record; irreversible

write_actions.name: create_webhook
write_actions.risk: registers a new outbound webhook that will POST live base-change notifications to an external URL of the caller's choosing; verify the target endpoint before enabling

write_actions.name: delete_webhook
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a webhook subscription; notification delivery to its target URL stops immediately

risk.read: external Airtable API read of base/table/record metadata
risk.write: external Airtable API mutation of records, table/field schema, comments, and webhooks; schema mutations (create_table/update_table/create_field/update_field) are visible to every base collaborator, approval required

name: akeneo
description: Reads Akeneo PIM products, categories, families, attributes, channels, product models, family variants, attribute groups, association types, locales, currencies, and measure families, and writes create-or-update upserts for the 9 catalog-structure resources, through the Akeneo REST API (OAuth2 password grant).

base_url.description: Akeneo PIM host URL (e.g. https://example.trial.akeneo.cloud). An absolute http(s) URL with a host is required; the connector fails closed otherwise (SSRF guard).

client_id.description: Akeneo OAuth2 API client ID (Basic-auth'd, paired with the client secret, on the token-exchange request only). Matches legacy's own config (non-secret) classification (internal/connectors/akeneo/akeneo.go's cfg.Config["client_id"]) even though it flows into an auth exchange -- never logged regardless.

secret.description: Akeneo OAuth2 API client secret, paired with client_id as HTTP Basic auth on the token-exchange request. Never logged.

api_username.description: Akeneo API user username, sent in the password-grant token-exchange JSON body. Matches legacy's own config (non-secret) classification -- never logged regardless.

password.description: Akeneo API user password, sent in the password-grant token-exchange JSON body. Never logged.

page_size.description: Records per page (1-100, the limit query param).

write_actions.name: create_or_update_product
write_actions.risk: creates a new product (201) or updates an existing one (204) in the connected Akeneo PIM catalog; visible to every downstream channel the product is enabled/categorized for

write_actions.name: create_or_update_category
write_actions.risk: creates or updates a category node; re-parenting an existing category changes the catalog tree for every product classified under it

write_actions.name: create_or_update_family
write_actions.risk: creates or updates a product family definition; changes the required/optional attribute set for every product assigned to this family

write_actions.name: create_or_update_attribute
write_actions.risk: creates a new attribute (schema mutation, affects every family/product referencing it) or updates an existing one's non-structural properties (labels/group); some attribute properties are immutable after creation per Akeneo's own API rules

write_actions.name: create_or_update_channel

write_actions.name: create_or_update_family_variant

write_actions.name: create_or_update_attribute_group

name: algolia
description: Reads Algolia indices, API keys, index settings, dictionaries, security sources, and logs, and writes index settings/API keys, through the Algolia Search REST API.

api_key.description: Algolia Admin API key, sent as the X-Algolia-API-Key header. Never logged.

application_id.description: Algolia application id, sent as the X-Algolia-Application-Id header and used to derive base_url when not overridden.

base_url.description: Algolia REST API base URL, e.g. https://<application_id>.algolia.net. Legacy derives this from application_id at runtime; this bundle requires it explicitly since the engine's spec-default mechanism only materializes a fixed literal, not an application_id-derived value (documented scope narrowing, see docs.md).

index_name.description: Algolia index name (required for the 'index_settings' stream).

write_actions.name: update_index_settings
write_actions.risk: overwrites the named index's search settings (ranking, faceting, searchable attributes); settings not included in the submitted record are left unchanged, but any included field replaces its current value immediately for live search traffic

write_actions.name: create_api_key
write_actions.risk: creates a new live Algolia API key with the requested ACL/index scope; a broadly-scoped key (e.g. admin-level ACLs) is a new standing credential that must be tracked and rotated like any other secret

risk.read: external Algolia API read of index/key/dictionary/security/log configuration metadata
risk.write: external mutation: overwrites live index search settings (update_index_settings) or creates a new standing API key credential (create_api_key); approval required
risk.approval: required for both write actions

name: alpaca-broker-api

username.description: Alpaca Broker API Key ID, sent as the HTTP Basic auth username.

password.description: Alpaca Broker API Secret Key, sent as the HTTP Basic auth password. Never logged.

base_url.description: Alpaca Broker API base URL. Defaults to the sandbox host, matching legacy's default when its 'environment' config is unset. Set to https://broker-api.alpaca.markets/v1 for production. Legacy also derives this from an 'environment' enum (api/paper-api/broker-api.sandbox) at runtime; this bundle requires the resolved URL directly since the engine's spec-default mechanism only materializes one fixed literal, not an enum-derived choice between two URLs (documented scope narrowing, see docs.md).

limit.description: Records per page for the 'accounts' stream (matches legacy's page_token cursor limit, defaultLimit=20).

risk.read: external Alpaca Broker API read of account/asset/market metadata, plus per-account trading positions, orders, watchlists, and document metadata (financial PII adjacent; no document content is downloaded, only listing metadata)

adjusted.description: Whether to return adjusted data. Only applicable to intraday endpoints.

base_url.description: Placeholder base URL used only to construct the engine runtime before the Tier-2 hook delegates to the legacy connector.

name: amazon-ads
description: Reads Amazon Advertising profiles, Sponsored Products campaigns, ad groups, product ads, keywords, negative keywords, and portfolios via the Amazon Ads API using a Login with Amazon (LWA) refresh-token grant. Read-only.

client_id.description: Login with Amazon (LWA) application client ID, used both as client_id in the refresh_token token exchange and verbatim in the Amazon-Advertising-API-ClientId header on every data request. Never logged.

client_secret.description: Login with Amazon (LWA) application client secret, used as client_secret in the refresh_token token exchange. Never logged.

refresh_token.description: Long-lived LWA refresh_token exchanged for a short-lived access_token on every Check/Read. Never logged.

base_url.description: Amazon Ads API base URL. Defaults to the North America (NA) endpoint, matching legacy's regionBaseURL["NA"] fallback. Legacy also derives this from a 'region' config enum (NA/EU/FE) at runtime; this bundle requires the resolved base_url directly for non-NA regions instead, since the engine's spec.json "default" mechanism only materializes one fixed literal, not a region-derived choice between three URLs (documented scope narrowing, see docs.md). Set to https://advertising-api-eu.amazon.com or https://advertising-api-fe.amazon.com for EU/FE accounts.

token_url.description: Login with Amazon token exchange endpoint override (matches legacy's regionTokenURL["NA"] default). Set to https://api.amazon.co.uk/auth/o2/token or https://api.amazon.co.jp/auth/o2/token for EU/FE accounts.

profile_id.description: Amazon Ads advertising profile ID. Required for every stream except profiles (which enumerates the accessible profiles/scopes itself); sent as the Amazon-Advertising-API-Scope header on profile-scoped streams (campaigns, ad_groups, portfolios, keywords), matching legacy's endpoint.scoped gate.

page_size.description: Records per page (startIndex/count offset pagination), 1-100. Matches legacy's defaultPageSize/maxPageSize.

max_pages.description: Maximum pages to read; 0, all, or unlimited exhausts the stream, matching legacy's amazonAdsMaxPages.

risk.read: external Amazon Ads API read of profile, campaign, ad group, product ad, keyword, negative keyword, and portfolio data
risk.approval: none; read-only, no reverse-ETL write surface

name: amazon-seller-partner
description: Reads Amazon Selling Partner API orders, inventory, finance, catalog, listings, fulfillment, reports, feeds, seller, shipping, vendor, and supporting JSON resources via Login with Amazon (LWA) authentication; exposes declarative writes for SP-API mutations that fit path/body JSON requests.

lwa_app_id.description: Login with Amazon (LWA) application client ID, used as client_id in the refresh_token token exchange. Never logged.

lwa_client_secret.description: Login with Amazon (LWA) application client secret, used as client_secret in the refresh_token token exchange. Never logged.

refresh_token.description: Long-lived LWA refresh_token exchanged for a short-lived access_token on every Check/Read. Never logged.

base_url.description: SP-API base URL. Defaults to the North America endpoint, matching legacy's spDefaultBaseURL/spDefaultBaseURL fallback. Legacy also derives this from a 'region' enum (NA/EU/FE and country codes) at runtime; this bundle requires the resolved base_url directly for non-NA regions since the engine's spec-default mechanism only materializes one fixed literal, not a region-derived choice between three URLs (documented scope narrowing, see docs.md). Set to https://sellingpartnerapi-eu.amazon.com or https://sellingpartnerapi-fe.amazon.com for EU/FE sellers.

lwa_token_url.description: Login with Amazon token exchange endpoint override (matches legacy's lwaDefaultTokenURL default).

marketplace_id.description: Amazon marketplace ID sent on Orders/FBA Inventory requests. Defaults to the US marketplace, matching legacy's defaultMarketplaceID.

replication_start_date.description: RFC3339 lower bound for time-windowed streams (orders, inventory_summaries, financial_event_groups) on a fresh sync with no incremental cursor yet, sent as LastUpdatedAfter/startDateTime/FinancialEventGroupStartedAfter respectively. REQUIRED here (unlike legacy): legacy's orders/financial_event_groups always compute a moving 'now minus 2 years' fallback (spDefaultCreatedAfter, re-evaluated via time.Now() on every call) when this is unset, which the engine's static spec.json/stream.Query default mechanisms cannot express (both bake a single fixed literal at bundle-author time, never a value relative to the current wall-clock time) — documented scope narrowing, see docs.md. Legacy's inventory_summaries never applies a fallback at all (it simply omits startDateTime when unset); requiring this field here is a strictly narrower config surface for that stream too, not a behavior change for any input where the field was already set.

page_size.description: Records per page for orders/financial_event_groups (1-100), matching legacy's spDefaultPageSize/spMaxPageSize. Not used by inventory_summaries (legacy's inventoryBaseQuery never sends a page-size param).

max_pages.description: Maximum pages to read; 0, all, or unlimited exhausts the stream, matching legacy's spMaxPages.

transaction_status.description: Optional transactions stream filter: one of Awin's documented status values (pending, approved, declined, deleted), sent verbatim as the status query parameter. Unset by default (no filter, matching legacy).

publisher_id.description: Optional transactions stream filter: a single publisher ID or Awin's documented comma-separated list of publisher IDs, sent verbatim as the publisherId query parameter. Unset by default (no filter, matching legacy).

name: bing-ads
description: Reads Microsoft Advertising (Bing Ads) accounts, users, campaigns, ad groups, and ads through the v13 Customer Management and Campaign Management REST APIs. Read-only.

client_id.description: Microsoft identity platform (Azure AD) application (client) ID for the refresh-token grant. Used only in the token-request form; never logged.

client_secret.description: Microsoft identity platform application client secret (optional for public/native client app registrations). Used only in the token-request form; never logged.

developer_token.description: Microsoft Advertising developer token, sent as the DeveloperToken header on every Customer/Campaign Management request; never logged.

refresh_token.description: Long-lived Microsoft identity platform OAuth 2.0 refresh token. Exchanged for a short-lived access token at token_url; never logged. The 3-legged consent/acquisition dance is out of scope for this connector (credentials layer already owns it).

tenant_id.description: Azure AD tenant id used to build the default token_url (https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant_id>/oauth2/v2.0/token). Defaults to 'common' when unset.

base_url.description: Customer Management REST service base URL override for tests or proxies.

campaign_base_url.description: Campaign Management REST service base URL override for tests or proxies. Campaign-scoped streams (campaigns, ad_groups, ads) target this service instead of base_url.

token_url.description: Microsoft identity platform OAuth 2.0 token endpoint override. Defaults to https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant_id>/oauth2/v2.0/token. MUST be https in production; the hook fails closed on a non-https or unparseable value.

customer_id.description: Microsoft Advertising CustomerId header/body scoping value, sent on Campaign Management requests and included in the accounts (AccountsInfo) query body when set.

customer_account_id.description: Microsoft Advertising CustomerAccountId header value for Campaign Management requests. Falls back to account_id when unset.

account_id.description: Single advertiser account id; used as the CustomerAccountId header fallback and as the sole AccountId when account_ids is unset.

account_ids.description: Comma-separated advertiser account ids. The campaigns stream fans out one QueryByAccountId request per id, stamping account_id onto every emitted record. Falls back to a single-element list from customer_account_id/account_id when unset.

campaign_id.description: Campaign id used to scope the ad_groups stream's AdGroups/QueryByCampaignId request body.

ad_group_id.description: Ad group id used to scope the ads stream's Ads/QueryByAdGroupId request body.

risk.read: external Microsoft Advertising REST API read of account/user/campaign/ad-group/ad metadata
risk.approval: none; read-only, no reverse-ETL write surface

name: braze
description: Reads Braze campaigns, Canvases, segments (list + per-id details/analytics-summary), catalogs, content blocks, email templates, Content Cards, email bounce/unsubscribe lists, SMS invalid-number lists, KPIs, sessions, preference centers, and scheduled broadcasts; writes user data (track/identify/merge/alias/delete), subscription-group status, catalog and catalog-item mutations, content block/email template mutations, email/SMS compliance-list mutations, preference center mutations, and live message/campaign/Canvas sends through the Braze REST API. The events (custom event names) and purchases/product_list streams are not modeled by this bundle; see docs.md Known limits.

api_key.description: Braze REST API key. Sent as Authorization: Bearer <api_key>. Never logged.

base_url.description: Your regional Braze REST endpoint, e.g. https://rest.iad-01.braze.com. Braze has no single global host, so this is required.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

write_actions.name: track_users
write_actions.risk: records user attribute/event/purchase data in bulk (up to 75 events/attributes/purchases per request per Braze's documented limit); an external user_id or user_alias in the record is the ONLY way Braze correlates the update to a user, so a mistargeted identifier silently attaches data to the wrong (or a newly-created) user profile

write_actions.name: identify_users
write_actions.risk: converts an anonymous/aliased user profile into an identified one and can merge attribute/behavior history onto the target identified profile; merge_behavior: merge combines the two profiles' full history irreversibly

write_actions.name: delete_users
write_actions.risk: permanently and irreversibly deletes user profiles and all their associated data (attributes, event/purchase history, message engagement); Braze does not offer an undelete path

write_actions.name: merge_users
write_actions.risk: irreversibly merges one user profile's full history into another and deletes the source profile identifier; up to 50 merge pairs per request per Braze's documented limit

write_actions.name: create_user_alias
write_actions.risk: creates new alias identifiers for existing (or new anonymous) user profiles; low-risk additive mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_user_alias
write_actions.risk: renames an existing alias identifier on a user profile; any external system correlating users by the old alias_name stops matching after this runs

write_actions.name: remove_user_external_ids
write_actions.risk: detaches an external_id from its user profile, converting that profile to anonymous; the profile itself is not deleted but becomes unreachable by the removed identifier

write_actions.name: rename_user_external_ids
write_actions.risk: renames a user's external_id; any external system correlating users by the old id stops matching after this runs

write_actions.name: set_subscription_status_v2
write_actions.risk: opts users into or out of an email/SMS subscription group in bulk (up to 50 groups x 50 identifiers per Braze's documented limit); setting subscription_state to unsubscribed on a transactional-adjacent group can stop legally-required or expected communications reaching those users

write_actions.name: create_catalog
write_actions.risk: creates a new catalog container with a fixed field schema; low-risk additive mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: delete_catalog
write_actions.risk: permanently deletes a catalog and every item it contains; any campaign/Canvas/Connected Content template referencing this catalog by name starts failing to resolve

write_actions.name: create_catalog_items
write_actions.risk: adds new rows (up to 50 per request per Braze's documented limit) to an existing catalog; low-risk additive mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_catalog_items
write_actions.risk: partially updates existing catalog rows in bulk by their id field; any Connected Content template or campaign personalization reading this catalog reflects the new values on its next fetch

write_actions.name: update_catalog_item
write_actions.risk: partially updates a single existing catalog row; any Connected Content template or campaign personalization reading this catalog reflects the new value on its next fetch

write_actions.name: delete_catalog_item
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a single row from a catalog; any Connected Content template or campaign personalization referencing this item_id starts returning no match

write_actions.name: create_content_block
write_actions.risk: creates a new reusable email Content Block; low-risk additive mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_content_block
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing Content Block's markup/text; changes are reflected in EVERY campaign/Canvas/template that includes this block on their next send, including already-scheduled sends

write_actions.name: create_email_template
write_actions.risk: creates a new reusable email template; low-risk additive mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_email_template
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing email template's subject/body; changes are reflected in EVERY campaign using this template on its next send, including already-scheduled sends

write_actions.name: create_email_blocklist
write_actions.risk: permanently blocklists email addresses from ever receiving Braze email again for this workspace; Braze's own docs note blocklisting cannot be undone via the API (requires a support request to reverse)

write_actions.name: remove_email_hard_bounce
write_actions.risk: clears an email address's hard-bounced status, allowing future sends to resume; use only after confirming the underlying delivery issue is actually resolved, or the address will likely hard-bounce again and harm sender reputation

write_actions.name: remove_email_spam
write_actions.risk: clears an email address's spam-complaint status, allowing future sends to resume; reversing a genuine spam complaint risks another complaint and further sender-reputation damage

write_actions.name: set_email_subscription_status
write_actions.risk: changes a single email address's global subscription state (subscribed/unsubscribed/opted_in); setting unsubscribed stops all future non-transactional email to that address

write_actions.name: remove_sms_invalid_phone_numbers
write_actions.risk: clears the invalid-number flag for phone numbers, allowing future SMS/MMS sends to resume; use only after confirming the number can actually receive messages again, or it will likely be re-flagged and waste sending budget

write_actions.name: create_preference_center
write_actions.risk: publishes a new customer-facing preference center page (a live, externally-reachable URL once active); low-risk additive mutation but review the submitted HTML before use since it is served to end users verbatim

write_actions.name: update_preference_center
write_actions.risk: overwrites an already-live, externally-reachable preference center page's HTML/title; visible to any end user who visits the page immediately after this runs

write_actions.name: send_message
write_actions.risk: immediately sends a live message (push/email/SMS/webhook/Content Card) to the specified users, segment, or broadcast audience; irreversible once dispatched and the single riskiest write this connector exposes — always confirm the audience scope (segment_id/audience filter vs. an explicit small external_user_ids list) before use

write_actions.name: trigger_campaign_send
write_actions.risk: immediately dispatches an existing API-triggered campaign to the specified recipients/audience; irreversible once dispatched, always confirm the recipients/audience scope before use

write_actions.name: trigger_canvas_send
write_actions.risk: immediately enters the specified recipients/audience into an existing API-triggered Canvas; irreversible once dispatched, always confirm the recipients/audience scope before use

risk.read: external Braze API read of campaign, Canvas, segment, catalog, content-block, template, Content-Card, email-compliance, SMS-compliance, KPI/session, and preference-center metadata
risk.write: external mutation of Braze user profiles (track/identify/merge/delete/alias), subscription-group membership, catalogs and catalog items, content blocks, email templates, email/SMS compliance lists, preference centers, and live message/campaign/Canvas sends; send_message/trigger_campaign_send/trigger_canvas_send dispatch real, irreversible communications to end users and delete_users/remove_user_external_ids/create_email_blocklist are destructive — every write ships with an explicit per-action risk string
risk.approval: required for destructive actions (delete_users, remove_user_external_ids, delete_catalog, delete_catalog_item, create_email_blocklist) and for any live send (send_message, trigger_campaign_send, trigger_canvas_send); catalog/content-block/template/preference-center create-update and compliance-list removals are lower-risk but still externally visible

write_actions.name: update_position

write_actions.name: update_candidate

Legacy discovers this dynamically on every read via GET /users/me (current_organization); the engine dialect has no mechanism to chain a prior request's response into a later request's query params, so this bundle asks the operator to configure the (per-account invariant) URI once instead — resolvable by calling GET https://api.calendly.com/users/me and reading resource.current_organization. See docs.md's Known limits.

base_url.description: Calendly API base URL override for tests or proxies.

start_date.description: RFC3339 lower bound; only scheduled_events starting at or after this time are read (Calendly's min_start_time filter). Other streams have no server-side lower-bound filter, matching legacy.

page_size.description: Records per page (1-100), sent as the count query param.

user_uri.description: The Calendly user URI whose availability schedules the user_availability_schedules stream reads (Calendly's `user` query filter is a required parameter naming one specific user, not the whole organization). Same per-account-invariant-value pattern as organization_uri: Calendly's API gives no 'list every user' endpoint and the engine dialect cannot chain a prior request's response into this one, so the operator configures it once — resolvable by calling GET https://api.calendly.com/users/me and reading resource.uri (the authenticated user's own URI is the common case). Required only for the user_availability_schedules stream; every other stream in this bundle is unaffected if it is left unset. See docs.md's Known limits.

Resolvable from the routing_forms stream's own uri field. Required only for the routing_form_submissions stream; every other stream in this bundle is unaffected if it is left unset. See docs.md's Known limits.

write_actions.name: create_role

name: drip
description: Reads Drip subscribers, campaigns, broadcasts, accounts, workflows, forms, tags, and webhooks, and writes subscriber/tag/broadcast/workflow/event/webhook mutations through the Drip REST API.

api_key.description: Drip API key. Sent as the HTTP Basic username with a blank password; never logged.

base_url.description: Drip API base URL override for tests or proxies.

account_id.description: Drip account ID; path-scopes the subscribers/campaigns/broadcasts streams (the accounts stream itself is account-agnostic).

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

write_actions.name: create_or_update_subscriber
write_actions.risk: creates a new subscriber or updates an existing one matched by email; low-risk external mutation, no approval required. Drip's real API strictly requires the one-subscriber-per-write body to still be an ARRAY under the "subscribers" key ({"subscribers": [{...}]}), not a bare object — record_schema's "subscribers" field is itself that array, and body_fields copies it verbatim so the wire body matches Drip's real shape exactly; the engine's schema dialect has no minItems/maxItems keyword to mechanically cap it to exactly one element, so callers are expected to supply exactly one (this action is not the true batch endpoint).

write_actions.name: delete_subscriber
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a subscriber and their event/tag history; destructive, approval required

write_actions.name: unsubscribe_subscriber
write_actions.risk: unsubscribes the named email from ALL mailings in the account; stops all future campaign/broadcast/workflow sends to them, approval required

write_actions.name: apply_tag
write_actions.risk: applies one or more tags to a subscriber, potentially triggering any workflow with a matching tag-applied trigger; low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: remove_tag
write_actions.risk: removes a tag from a subscriber, potentially triggering any workflow with a matching tag-removed trigger; low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: record_event
write_actions.risk: records a custom behavioral event on a subscriber, which can trigger any workflow with a matching event trigger; low-risk external mutation, no approval required. Drip's real API requires the body to be an ARRAY under the "events" key even for one event; record_schema's "events" field is itself that array (callers are expected to supply exactly one element; this action is not the true batch endpoint).

write_actions.name: create_broadcast
write_actions.risk: creates a new draft single-email campaign (broadcast); low-risk in draft form (not sent), no approval required. Drip's real API requires the body to be an ARRAY under the "broadcasts" key even for one broadcast; record_schema's "broadcasts" field is itself that array (callers are expected to supply exactly one element; this action is not the true batch endpoint).

write_actions.name: update_broadcast
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing draft broadcast's subject/content; Drip only allows updating broadcasts still in draft status, so this cannot alter an already-sent email; external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: delete_broadcast
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a broadcast; destructive if it was already sent (removes historical record, though delivered emails cannot be recalled), approval required

write_actions.name: activate_workflow
write_actions.risk: activates a paused workflow, resuming automated sends to everyone currently enrolled and allowing new triggers to enroll people; external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: pause_workflow
write_actions.risk: pauses an active workflow, stopping automated sends to everyone currently enrolled and disabling new triggers; low-risk (reversible via activate_workflow), no approval required

write_actions.name: create_webhook
write_actions.risk: registers a new outbound webhook that will POST live subscriber/campaign event data to an external URL of the caller's choosing; verify the target endpoint before enabling. Drip's real API requires the body to be an ARRAY under the "webhooks" key even for one webhook; record_schema's "webhooks" field is itself that array (callers are expected to supply exactly one element; this action is not the true batch endpoint).

write_actions.name: delete_webhook
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a webhook subscription; stops future event delivery to its post_url; destructive, approval required

risk.read: external Drip API read of subscriber, campaign, broadcast, account, workflow, form, tag, and webhook data
risk.write: external Drip API mutation of subscribers, tags, broadcasts, workflows, custom events, and webhooks; delete_subscriber and delete_broadcast/delete_webhook are destructive and require approval
risk.approval: required for delete_subscriber, delete_broadcast, delete_webhook, and unsubscribe_subscriber; tag/event/workflow-state writes are lower-risk and do not require approval

write_actions.name: remove_signature_request

write_actions.name: delete_template

write_actions.name: remove_template_user

write_actions.name: update_team

write_actions.name: remove_team_member

risk.write: external mutation of signature requests (update/cancel/remind/release_hold/remove), templates (delete/add_user/remove_user), teams (create/update/add_member/remove_member), and account settings; several actions are destructive/not reversible (cancel_signature_request, remove_signature_request, delete_template, remove_team_member) and require approval

name: dwolla
description: Reads Dwolla customers, events, exchange partners, and business classifications, and writes customer/funding-source/transfer/webhook-subscription/beneficial-owner lifecycle mutations, via the Dwolla HAL+JSON REST API using OAuth2 client-credentials.

write_actions.name: create_customer
write_actions.risk: external mutation; creates a new Dwolla customer (personal, business, receive-only, or unverified), subject to Dwolla's identity-verification rules for the requested type

write_actions.name: update_customer
write_actions.risk: external mutation; updates a customer's profile fields, or its status (e.g. deactivating/reactivating the customer, which blocks/restores its ability to transact)

write_actions.name: create_funding_source
write_actions.risk: external mutation; attaches a new bank-account funding source to a customer, either as unverified (routingNumber/accountNumber, requiring later micro-deposit verification) or pre-verified via an open-banking plaidToken/onDemandAuthorizationId

write_actions.name: update_funding_source
write_actions.risk: external mutation; renames a funding source or replaces its unverified bank-account routing/account numbers

write_actions.name: remove_funding_source
write_actions.risk: destructive external mutation; Dwolla has no hard-delete for funding sources, this soft-removes it (POST {removed:true}) so it can no longer send/receive transfers; not reversible via the API

write_actions.risk: external mutation; sends two small trial-deposit ACH transactions to an unverified bank-account funding source, the first step of micro-deposit verification

write_actions.name: verify_micro_deposits
write_actions.risk: external mutation; verifies a funding source's micro-deposit amounts, completing bank-account verification; Dwolla locks the funding source after repeated failed attempts

write_actions.name: cancel_transfer
write_actions.risk: external mutation; cancels a still-pending transfer before it clears, this action is not reversible and only succeeds while the transfer's status is pending

write_actions.name: create_webhook_subscription
write_actions.risk: external mutation; registers a new webhook subscription; Dwolla enforces a maximum of 10 active subscriptions in Sandbox and 5 in Production

write_actions.name: update_webhook_subscription
write_actions.risk: external mutation; pauses or resumes webhook delivery for a subscription (Dwolla still generates the events while paused, it just withholds delivery)

write_actions.name: delete_webhook_subscription
write_actions.risk: destructive external mutation; permanently deletes a webhook subscription and stops all future event delivery to it; not reversible

write_actions.name: create_beneficial_owner
write_actions.risk: external mutation; registers a beneficial owner (25%+ equity holder) for a business verified customer; submits sensitive PII (SSN, date of birth, address) to Dwolla for identity verification

write_actions.name: update_beneficial_owner
write_actions.risk: external mutation; updates a beneficial owner's identity/PII fields, which resets its verification status pending re-review

write_actions.name: remove_beneficial_owner
write_actions.risk: destructive external mutation; permanently removes a beneficial owner from a business verified customer; not reversible and may affect the customer's beneficial-ownership certification status

write_actions.name: certify_beneficial_ownership

write_actions.name: update_supplier

write_actions.name: update_task

write_actions.name: delete_section

name: exchange-rates
description: Reads latest, currency-conversion, time-series, and fluctuation foreign-exchange rate data from the exchangeratesapi.io REST API. The legacy exchange_rates daily-historical stream (a date-by-date iteration over a start_date..end_date window) and the symbols stream are not ported; see docs.md Known limits.

access_key.description: exchangeratesapi.io access key, sent as the access_key query parameter. Never logged.

base_url.description: Exchange Rates API base URL override for tests or proxies.

base.description: Optional base currency code applied to the latest and symbols requests (the API's optional 'base' query parameter).

convert_from.description: Source currency code for the convert stream (the API's required 'from' query parameter). Only read when the convert stream itself is synced.

convert_to.description: Target currency code for the convert stream (the API's required 'to' query parameter). Only read when the convert stream itself is synced.

convert_amount.description: Amount to convert for the convert stream (the API's required 'amount' query parameter, sent verbatim as a string). Only read when the convert stream itself is synced.

convert_date.description: Optional historical date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the convert stream (the API's optional 'date' query parameter); omitted for a live-rate conversion when unset.

timeseries_start_date.description: Inclusive window start date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the timeseries stream (the API's required 'start_date' query parameter). Only read when the timeseries stream itself is synced.

timeseries_end_date.description: Inclusive window end date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the timeseries stream (the API's required 'end_date' query parameter). Only read when the timeseries stream itself is synced.

fluctuation_start_date.description: Inclusive window start date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the fluctuation stream (the API's required 'start_date' query parameter). Only read when the fluctuation stream itself is synced.

fluctuation_end_date.description: Inclusive window end date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the fluctuation stream (the API's required 'end_date' query parameter). Only read when the fluctuation stream itself is synced.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

risk.read: external exchangeratesapi.io read of public foreign-exchange rate data
risk.approval: none; read-only public data API

risk.read: external GitBook API reads across users, organizations, spaces, sites, content, permissions, integrations, analytics, search, and related resources
risk.write: creates, updates, publishes, archives, deletes, imports, exports, invites, permission changes, and content changes in GitBook depending on the selected write action
risk.approval: reverse ETL writes require plan preview and approval token before execution

name: github
description: Reads GitHub repository, issue, pull request, code, release, collaboration, Actions, security (code scanning/dependabot/secret scanning/advisories), webhook, deploy key, environment, and ruleset data, and writes approved reverse ETL actions through the GitHub REST API (full-surface certified: 37 streams, 231 write actions accounted).

owner.description: Repository owner (user or organization login). Legacy accepted a single "owner/repo" repository config value and split it at runtime; the engine's path templating urlencodes each {{ }} reference as one opaque path segment (a literal "/" would be percent-encoded, not treated as a segment delimiter), so owner and repo are declared as two separate config keys instead.

repo.description: Repository name (without the owner prefix). See owner's description for why this is a separate config key from legacy's single repository field.

base_url.description: GitHub API base URL override for tests or GitHub Enterprise.

installation_id.description: GitHub App installation ID for auth_type=github_app.

installation_repositories.description: Optional comma-separated repository names for a restricted installation token.

installation_repository_ids.description: Optional comma-separated repository IDs for a restricted installation token.

installation_permissions.description: Optional JSON object of requested GitHub App installation-token permissions.

public_access.description: Explicit opt-in for unauthenticated (public) reads. Set to any non-empty value (e.g. 'true') to allow reads with no token/app credentials configured. Leaving this unset (and auth_type unset/not one of the public synonyms below) requires a token secret or app_id+installation_id+private_key to authenticate; a config with none of those AND no explicit public opt-in hard-errors rather than silently falling back to an unauthenticated read (F4 fail-loud deviation from legacy's auth_type=auto resolution, which DOES silently fall through to public — see docs.md Known limits/ledger G14). This is the PRIMARY documented opt-in surface (the resulting behavior — explicit opt-in required, no silent fallthrough — is what the legacy behavior SHOULD have been from a fail-loud standpoint); auth_type (below) is an additional, purely-additive way to reach the identical mode:none outcome for callers migrating a legacy auth_type=public-shaped config verbatim.

auth_type.description: Legacy's auth_type string-enum surface (auth.go:81-82), restored ADDITIONALLY alongside public_access once engine.ResolveCheckWhen made the when-grammar's `in` operator statically validatable (S3 engine mini-wave item 2, ledger G14 R1 CONDITION). Only the 4 legacy PUBLIC synonyms are reproduced here — 'public', 'none', 'anonymous', or 'unauthenticated' (case-sensitive; legacy lowercases/normalizes before comparing, this bundle does not) arm the identical mode:none candidate public_access arms. Legacy's OTHER auth_type values (token/oauth/github_app/etc. synonyms, and auth_type=github_app's override-token-precedence behavior) are NOT reproduced — this key exists solely to close the public-enum migration gap, not to replicate legacy's full auth_type mode-selection semantics; any other auth_type value (or none at all) has zero effect on auth selection, which still resolves via the token/app_id-presence candidates ahead of it in the auth list.

since.description: Lower-bound timestamp for issues, issue_comments, and pull_request_review_comments (incremental start; also usable as a fresh-sync start_config_key value).

token.description: GitHub token: classic PAT, fine-grained PAT, OAuth token, GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN, or a pre-generated installation access token. Used only for Bearer auth; never logged.

private_key.description: GitHub App PEM private key for auth_type=github_app. Never logged.

private_key_base64.description: Base64-encoded GitHub App PEM private key for auth_type=github_app (alternative to private_key). Never logged.

risk.read: external API read
risk.write: external GitHub API mutation
risk.approval: reverse ETL plan approval required before writes

name: gitlab
description: Reads GitLab projects, groups, users, and issues through the GitLab REST API v4.

access_token.description: GitLab personal access token or OAuth access token. Used only for Bearer auth; never logged.

base_url.description: GitLab API base URL override, e.g. https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4 for self-managed instances, or for tests/proxies.

start_date.description: RFC3339 lower bound applied as each stream's matching since-filter (last_activity_after for projects, created_after for users, updated_after for issues; groups has no since-filter upstream).

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

risk.read: external GitLab API read of projects, groups, users, and issues

name: glassfrog
description: Reads GlassFrog circles, roles, people, projects, and assignments through the GlassFrog API v3 (read-only full-refresh source).

api_key.description: GlassFrog API token, sent as the X-Auth-Token header. Never logged.

base_url.description: GlassFrog API base URL override for tests or proxies.

risk.read: external GlassFrog API read of circle, role, person, project, and assignment data
risk.approval: none; read-only, no obviously-safe reverse-ETL writes

name: gmail
description: Reads Gmail messages, threads, drafts, labels, history, filters, send-as aliases, delegates, forwarding addresses, and mailbox profile, and writes approved reverse-ETL mutations (send/insert/import/modify/trash/delete messages and threads; draft and label lifecycle; filter, send-as, delegate, and forwarding-address management; vacation/language/IMAP/POP/auto-forwarding settings) via the Google OAuth 2.0 refresh-token grant.

client_id.description: Google OAuth 2.0 client ID for the refresh-token grant. Used only in the token-request form; never logged.

client_secret.description: Google OAuth 2.0 client secret (optional for some client types). Used only in the token-request form; never logged.

client_refresh_token.description: Long-lived Google OAuth 2.0 refresh token. Exchanged for a short-lived access token at token_url; never logged. The 3-legged consent/acquisition dance is out of scope for this connector (credentials layer already owns it).

base_url.description: Gmail API base URL override for tests or proxies.

token_url.description: Google OAuth 2.0 token endpoint override. MUST be https in production; the hook fails closed on a non-https or unparseable value to prevent exfiltrating the refresh token to an attacker-chosen endpoint.

scopes.description: OAuth scope requested on the token-refresh grant. Pass B widens the default from the wave1-pilot read-only gmail.readonly scope to the full https://mail.google.com/ scope, since this bundle now declares mutating write actions (send/modify/trash/delete/settings) that gmail.readonly cannot authorize; narrow this back to a read-only scope string if only the streams in this bundle are ever used.

user_id.description: Gmail user ID path segment (email address for delegated access, or 'me').

start_date.description: RFC3339 lower bound; translated to a Gmail search query 'after:<unix-seconds>' filter. Not a true incremental cursor: messages/threads/drafts list endpoints are newest-first and publish no cursor field, matching legacy.

include_spam_and_trash.description: When 'true', includes SPAM and TRASH in list results (includeSpamTrash=true). Unset keeps Gmail's default exclusion, matching legacy's omitted-param false default.

start_history_id.description: Gmail historyId lower bound for the history stream's incremental sync (users.history.list's required startHistoryId). Unlike messages/threads/drafts, history genuinely publishes a server-recognized, monotonically-increasing cursor (historyId) -- see Streams notes in docs.md. Obtain an initial value from any message/thread/label/profile record's historyId field.

write_actions.name: send_message
write_actions.risk: sends a real outbound email on behalf of the mailbox owner; irreversible once delivered

write_actions.name: insert_message
write_actions.risk: inserts a message directly into the mailbox without sending it (no SMTP delivery, no notifications) -- still a real, visible mailbox mutation

write_actions.name: import_message
write_actions.risk: imports a message into the mailbox from an external mail migration source, bypassing spam classification by default

write_actions.name: modify_message
write_actions.risk: changes label state on an existing message (e.g. moving in/out of INBOX/TRASH/UNREAD), visible to the mailbox owner

write_actions.name: trash_message
write_actions.risk: moves a message to Trash; auto-purged by Gmail after 30 days

write_actions.name: untrash_message
write_actions.risk: restores a trashed message back to its prior labels

write_actions.name: delete_message
write_actions.risk: permanently deletes a message immediately, bypassing Trash; irreversible

write_actions.name: modify_thread
write_actions.risk: changes label state on every message in an existing thread

write_actions.name: trash_thread
write_actions.risk: moves an entire thread to Trash; auto-purged by Gmail after 30 days

write_actions.name: untrash_thread
write_actions.risk: restores a trashed thread back to its prior labels

write_actions.name: delete_thread
write_actions.risk: permanently deletes every message in a thread immediately, bypassing Trash; irreversible

write_actions.name: create_draft
write_actions.risk: creates a new unsent draft, visible to the mailbox owner

write_actions.name: update_draft
write_actions.risk: replaces the entire content of an existing draft

write_actions.name: send_draft
write_actions.risk: sends a real outbound email from an existing draft on behalf of the mailbox owner; irreversible once delivered

write_actions.name: delete_draft
write_actions.risk: permanently deletes a draft; irreversible

write_actions.name: create_label
write_actions.risk: creates a new custom label visible in the mailbox owner's label list

write_actions.name: update_label
write_actions.risk: replaces the full definition of an existing label (name/visibility/color); a system label's name cannot actually be changed by Gmail even though the request is accepted

write_actions.name: patch_label
write_actions.risk: partially updates an existing label's fields, leaving unset fields unchanged

write_actions.name: delete_label
write_actions.risk: removes a user label from the account and from every message/thread that carried it; system labels reject deletion with an error

write_actions.name: create_filter
write_actions.risk: creates a mail filter that automatically acts on future incoming messages matching its criteria (may auto-forward mail externally)

write_actions.name: delete_filter
write_actions.risk: removes an existing mail filter; future messages stop being auto-actioned by it

write_actions.name: create_send_as
write_actions.risk: adds a new custom From: alias; Google emails a verification link to the new address before it can send mail

write_actions.name: update_send_as
write_actions.risk: replaces the full send-as alias configuration, including which alias is the account default

write_actions.name: patch_send_as
write_actions.risk: partially updates an existing send-as alias, leaving unset fields unchanged

write_actions.name: delete_send_as
write_actions.risk: removes a custom From: alias (the account's primary address cannot be deleted; Gmail rejects that request)

write_actions.name: verify_send_as
write_actions.risk: re-sends the verification email for a pending custom From: alias

write_actions.name: create_delegate

description: Reads Google Analytics 4 reports (active users, traffic sources, devices, pages) from the Analytics Data API runReport endpoint. Read-only. In architecture v2 this quarantine bundle dispatches live reads through a Tier-2 hook that delegates to the legacy connector until the wave 6 cutover.

convert_conversions_event.description: Enables conversion of `conversions:*` event metrics from integers to floats. This is beneficial for preventing data rounding when the API returns float values for any `conversions:*` fields.

custom_reports_array.description: You can add your Custom Analytics report by creating one.

date_ranges_end_date.description: The end date from which to replicate report data in the format YYYY-MM-DD. Data generated after this date will not be included in the report. Not applied to custom Cohort reports. When no date is provided or the date is in the future, the date from today is used.

date_ranges_start_date.description: The start date from which to replicate report data in the format YYYY-MM-DD. Data generated before this date will not be included in the report. Not applied to custom Cohort reports.

keep_empty_rows.description: If false, each row with all metrics equal to 0 will not be returned. If true, these rows will be returned if they are not separately removed by a filter. More information is available in the documentation.

lookback_window.description: Since attribution changes after the event date, and Google Analytics has a data processing latency, we should specify how many days in the past we should refresh the data in every run. So if you set it at 5 days, in every sync it will fetch the last bookmark date minus 5 days.

property_ids.description: A list of your Property IDs. The Property ID is a unique number assigned to each property in Google Analytics, found in your GA4 property URL. This ID allows the connector to track the specific events associated with your property. Refer to the Google Analytics documentation to locate your property ID.

subscription_tier.description: Quota tier of the Google Analytics 4 properties being queried. Determines the per-property rate-limit policy applied locally once the tier-aware rate-limit budget is activated. Select "Analytics 360 Property" only if all configured property IDs belong to an Analytics 360 subscription. See https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/quotas.

base_url.description: Full Linear GraphQL endpoint URL override for tests or proxies. Must be the complete endpoint (including any path); unlike legacy, a bare-host override is NOT auto-suffixed with /graphql by this bundle (see docs.md Known limits). Defaults to https://api.linear.app/graphql.

api_key.description: Linear personal API key, sent as a bare Authorization header (no Bearer prefix). Provide either api_key or access_token.

access_token.description: Linear OAuth access token, sent as a Bearer Authorization header. Provide either api_key or access_token; access_token takes priority when both are set.

auth_type.description: Optional. Set to oauth or oauth2.0 to send api_key with a Bearer prefix instead of the default bare personal-API-key header (legacy's isOAuth config-forced-Bearer path). Not needed when access_token is set (access_token always uses Bearer regardless of this value).

page_size.description: GraphQL connection page size (1-250, Linear's own cap). Hooks-consumed; see docs.md Known limits.

max_pages.description: Optional hard cap on the number of pages read per stream. Empty, "all", or "unlimited" means unbounded (the default). Hooks-consumed; see docs.md Known limits.

risk.read: external Linear GraphQL API read of issues/teams/projects/users
risk.approval: none; read-only source connector

name: linkedin-ads
description: Reads LinkedIn Ads accounts, campaign groups, campaigns, and creatives through the LinkedIn Marketing REST API.

access_token.description: LinkedIn member OAuth2 access token (resolved from legacy's credentials.access_token secret). Sent as a Bearer token; never logged. The refresh_token exchange is performed outside this connector.

base_url.description: LinkedIn Marketing API base URL override for tests or proxies.

linkedin_version.description: LinkedIn-Version header value (monthly, YYYYMM). Defaults to the connector's built-in version.

max_pages.description: Maximum pages; use 0, all, or unlimited to exhaust the stream.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

risk.read: external LinkedIn Marketing API read of ad account, campaign, and creative data

name: linkedin-pages
description: Reads LinkedIn organization (company page) profile, follower statistics, share statistics, and total follower count through the LinkedIn Community Management REST API.

org_id.description: LinkedIn organization id (company page). Scopes every request and is stamped onto every emitted record. Not a credential (a bare numeric organization identifier); declared as ordinary config, not x-secret, so it is available to computed_fields (secrets.* is never wired into computed_fields templating, see conventions.md §3) and to the request path/query.

access_token.description: LinkedIn member OAuth2 access token (long-lived). The refresh_token exchange, when needed, is performed by the operator/agent layer before this connector runs; only the resolved bearer token is used here.

base_url.description: LinkedIn Community Management API base URL override for tests or proxies.

linkedin_version.description: LinkedIn-Version header value (YYYYMM). LinkedIn versions are monthly.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

risk.read: external LinkedIn Community Management API read of company page profile and lifetime statistics
risk.approval: none; read-only, no reverse-ETL write surface

name: outlook
description: Reads Outlook messages, mail folders, and calendar events through Microsoft Graph using an OAuth 2.0 refresh-token grant.

client_id.description: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) application (client) ID for the OAuth 2.0 refresh-token grant. Used only in the token-request form; never logged.

client_secret.description: Microsoft Entra ID application client secret. Used only in the token-request form; never logged.

refresh_token.description: Long-lived Microsoft Graph OAuth 2.0 refresh token. Exchanged for a short-lived access token at token_url; never logged. The 3-legged consent/acquisition dance is out of scope for this connector (credentials layer already owns it).

base_url.description: Microsoft Graph API base URL override for tests or proxies.

token_url.description: Microsoft identity platform token endpoint override. When unset, it is derived from tenant_id (https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}/oauth2/v2.0/token, tenant_id defaulting to "common"). MUST be an https URL with a host; the hook fails closed on an invalid value to prevent exfiltrating the refresh token/client secret to an attacker-chosen endpoint.

tenant_id.description: Microsoft Entra ID tenant ID (or "common"/"organizations"/"consumers"), used to derive token_url when token_url is not set directly.

scope.description: OAuth 2.0 scope(s) requested in the token exchange (space-separated). Optional; omitted from the token request entirely when unset.

max_pages.description: Maximum pages; use 0, all, or unlimited to exhaust the stream.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

risk.read: external Microsoft Graph API read of the authenticated mailbox's messages, mail folders, and calendar events
risk.approval: none; read-only, no reverse-ETL write surface

organization_name.description: Picqer subdomain; the connector always derives https://<organization_name>.picqer.com/api/v1 from it. mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

write_actions.name: update_return

write_actions.name: delete_return

name: retailexpress-by-maropost
description: Reads Retail Express products, customers, orders, stock levels, and stores through the Maropost API. Read-only.

spec.title: Retail Express by Maropost Connection Specification

base_url.description: Retail Express account base URL, e.g. https://<account>.retailexpress.com.au/api/v2. Legacy derives this from a bare `account` config alias when base_url is unset; this bundle requires the full base_url instead (see docs.md Known limits).

access_token.description: OAuth-style access token, sent as a Bearer token. Takes priority over api_key when both are configured, matching legacy's access-token-first precedence. Never logged.

api_key.description: API key, sent as the X-API-Key header. Used only when access_token is not configured. Never logged.

updated_after.description: Optional updated-after filter applied to every stream's request, matching legacy's config-driven query filter.

created_after.description: Optional created-after filter applied to every stream's request.

store_id.description: Optional store ID filter applied to every stream's request.

status.description: Optional status filter applied to every stream's request.

risk.read: external Retail Express by Maropost API read of product, customer, order, and stock data

name: retently
description: Reads Retently customers, survey responses, surveys, and campaigns through the REST API.

api_key.description: Retently API v2 key, sent as an Authorization: api_key=<api_key> header (legacy's connsdk.APIKeyHeader convention). Never logged.

base_url.description: Retently API base URL override for tests or proxies.

updated_after.description: Optional passthrough filter: only return customers/surveys/campaigns updated at or after this value.

created_after.description: Optional passthrough filter: only return responses created at or after this value.

email.description: Optional passthrough filter: scope the customers stream to a single customer email.

campaign_id.description: Optional passthrough filter: scope the responses stream to a single campaign id.

risk.read: external Retently API read of customer and NPS/CSAT survey response data

name: revenuecat
description: Reads and writes RevenueCat v2 project configuration, customer, product, offering, subscription, purchase, paywall, virtual currency, integration, and metrics resources through the REST API.

api_key.description: RevenueCat secret API key, sent as an Authorization: Bearer <api_key> header. Never logged.

base_url.description: RevenueCat API base URL override for tests or proxies.

project_id.description: RevenueCat project id. Required by the apps/products/offerings/customers streams (project-scoped resources); not required by the projects stream itself, matching legacy's per-stream project_id check.

starting_after.description: Optional passthrough filter: cursor id to resume a customers/apps/products/offerings listing after.

created_after.description: Optional passthrough filter: only return records created at or after this value.

updated_after.description: Optional passthrough filter: only return records updated at or after this value.

app_id.description: RevenueCat app id for app detail, API-key, and StoreKit config streams.

customer_id.description: RevenueCat customer id for customer detail and customer-scoped streams.

entitlement_id.description: RevenueCat entitlement id for entitlement detail/product streams.

offering_id.description: RevenueCat offering id for offering detail/package streams.

package_id.description: RevenueCat package id for package detail/product streams.

product_id.description: RevenueCat product id for product detail streams.

purchase_id.description: RevenueCat purchase id for purchase detail streams.

subscription_id.description: RevenueCat subscription id for subscription detail streams.

invoice_id.description: RevenueCat invoice id for invoice-related operations.

webhook_integration_id.description: RevenueCat webhook integration id for webhook detail streams.

paywall_id.description: RevenueCat paywall id for paywall detail streams.

virtual_currency_code.description: RevenueCat virtual currency code for virtual currency detail streams.

chart_name.description: RevenueCat chart name for chart data and chart option streams.

store_purchase_identifier.description: Store purchase identifier used by the purchases search endpoint.

store_subscription_identifier.description: Store subscription identifier used by the subscriptions search endpoint.

write_actions.name: update_addressbook

write_actions.name: add_emails_to_book

write_actions.name: remove_emails_from_book

write_actions.name: create_campaign

write_actions.name: cancel_campaign

write_actions.name: remove_sender

write_actions.name: add_to_blacklist

write_actions.name: remove_from_blacklist
write_actions.risk: removes an address from the account-wide suppression list; future campaigns can reach it again

risk.write: external SendPulse API mutation, including creating email campaigns that may send to real subscribers

write_actions.name: create_incident
write_actions.risk: creates a new incident record; low-risk external mutation (a new ticket), no approval required

write_actions.name: create_user
write_actions.risk: creates a new ServiceNow user account record; a new user account granted whatever role/ACL defaults the instance applies is a higher-scrutiny mutation than an incident/group create

write_actions.name: create_group
write_actions.risk: creates a new user group record; low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_incident
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing incident's recorded fields (only fields present in the submitted record are changed; ServiceNow's Table API PATCH/PUT both modify only the submitted fields, never the whole record) by sys_id

write_actions.name: update_user
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing user account's profile fields by sys_id, including active (deactivating a user's account revokes their instance access); higher-scrutiny than incident/group updates

write_actions.name: update_group
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing group's recorded fields by sys_id, including active/manager; can change who is considered the group's membership owner

risk.read: external ServiceNow API read of incident, user, and group table data
risk.write: creates incident/user/group records and updates their fields by sys_id (ServiceNow Table API PATCH, which modifies only submitted fields); creating/deactivating a user account is a higher-scrutiny mutation than incident/group create-update
risk.approval: none for incident/group create-update (low-risk ticketing/CRM-style data); review user create/update before enabling in a caller with untrusted input, since it can grant or revoke ServiceNow instance access

name: sharetribe
description: Reads and writes Sharetribe listings, users, transactions, availability, stock, and marketplace data through the Sharetribe Integration API.

oauth_access_token.description: Sharetribe Integration API OAuth2 access token, sent as a Bearer token. Never logged.

base_url.description: Sharetribe Integration API base URL override for tests or proxies.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

write_actions.name: create_listing
write_actions.risk: creates a new marketplace listing; low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_listing
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing listing's details by id; cannot be used to change listing state (use close_listing/open_listing/approve_listing for that); publicData/privateData/metadata are merged with the existing object on the top level, not deep-merged

write_actions.name: close_listing
write_actions.risk: sets the listing's state to closed; it stops being discoverable via the public Marketplace API listings/query endpoint but remains reachable by id or through related transactions

write_actions.name: open_listing
write_actions.risk: sets a closed listing's state back to published, making it publicly discoverable again; low-risk, no approval required

write_actions.name: approve_listing
write_actions.risk: approves a listing currently in pendingApproval state, setting it to published and making it publicly visible; review before enabling in a caller with untrusted input if the marketplace relies on manual listing moderation

write_actions.name: approve_user
write_actions.risk: approves a pending user account, setting its state to active and granting it marketplace access; higher-scrutiny than listing writes since it grants account access

write_actions.name: update_user_profile
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing user's profile fields by id; publicData/protectedData/privateData/metadata are merged with the existing object on the top level, not deep-merged

write_actions.name: update_user_permissions
write_actions.risk: changes what a user is permitted to do on the marketplace (post listings, initiate transactions, read); a higher-scrutiny access-control mutation, review before enabling in a caller with untrusted input

write_actions.name: verify_user_email
write_actions.risk: marks the given email address as verified for the user; low-risk account-state mutation

write_actions.name: transition_transaction
write_actions.risk: transitions a real transaction to a new state via the marketplace's transaction process (e.g. accepting/declining a booking, marking payment); only operator-actor transitions are permitted; a maximum of 100 transitions per transaction; can trigger real payment capture/payout actions depending on the process definition

write_actions.name: transition_transaction_speculative
write_actions.risk: simulates a transaction transition to validate parameters or preview the resulting price breakdown; the transaction state is NOT actually changed — safe to call freely, no approval required

write_actions.name: update_transaction_metadata
write_actions.risk: mutates an existing transaction's metadata (merged with the existing object on the top level, not deep-merged); low-risk, does not affect payment/process state

write_actions.name: create_availability_exception
write_actions.risk: overrides a listing's availability plan for a given time range (e.g. blocking it out or opening extra seats); low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: delete_availability_exception
write_actions.risk: permanently removes an availability exception by id, restoring the listing's default availability plan for that time range

write_actions.name: set_listing_stock
write_actions.risk: sets a listing's total available stock via a compare-and-set (only applied if the listing's current stock matches oldTotal); low-risk external mutation, no approval required

write_actions.name: create_stock_adjustment
write_actions.risk: creates an immutable stock adjustment for a listing (increases or decreases available stock by quantity); low-risk external mutation, no approval required

risk.read: external Sharetribe Integration API read of listing, user, transaction, event, marketplace, file, and file-attachment data
risk.write: creates/updates/closes/opens/approves listings, approves/updates users and their permissions, transitions transactions (including real payment/payout process actions), manages availability exceptions and listing stock
risk.approval: none for listing/user-profile/stock/availability-exception mutations (reversible, low-risk marketplace-operator actions); review transition_transaction and update_user_permissions before enabling in a caller with untrusted input, since transitions can trigger real payment capture/payout and permission changes affect account access
