to_date.description: Optional SVTODATE (YYYYMMDD) upper bound applied to the vouchers stream. Ignored by the master streams.

name: vwo
description: Reads and writes VWO (Visual Website Optimizer) A/B testing campaigns.

base_url.description: VWO API base URL. Defaults to the public VWO API v2 host (confirmed current and correct against the live OpenAPI spec published at developers.wingify.com, which documents the identical https://app.wingify.com/api/v2 host family).

api_key.description: VWO personal API token, generated at https://app.wingify.com/#/developers/tokens. Pass B correction: the real, currently-documented API's OpenAPI security scheme is an apiKey header named 'token' (bare token value, no prefix) -- sent as 'token: <api_key>' -- NOT the 'Authorization: Token <api_key>' shape this bundle previously (and legacy) sent. Never logged.

account_id.description: VWO workspace/account id used as the {account_id} path segment on every request (Pass B correction: the real API's campaigns endpoints are ALWAYS account-scoped, e.g. /accounts/{account_id}/campaigns -- legacy's bare /campaigns path targeted a URL shape the real API does not expose). Defaults to the literal 'current', VWO's own documented keyword for 'the Main Workspace of the authenticated token' -- so no additional required config is introduced versus legacy's zero-config behavior. Set to a specific numeric workspace id to target a sub-account instead.

start_date.description: Optional start_date query parameter passed through to the campaigns endpoint verbatim (RFC3339). Not used as a stateful incremental cursor by legacy. NOTE: this is not a real VWO query parameter (the real 'Get all campaigns' endpoint has no date-range filter at all -- see docs.md); it is preserved here only for config-shape backward compatibility with the original migration and is a silent no-op against the real API, same as it always effectively was.

campaign_type.description: Optional campaign-type filter, sent as the real API's 'type' query parameter only when configured (Pass B full-surface expansion of the campaigns endpoint's documented type filter).

platform.description: Optional platform filter, sent as the real API's 'platform' query parameter only when configured (Pass B full-surface expansion).

page_size.description: Sent as the real API's 'limit' query parameter (Pass B full-surface expansion). VWO's documented default is 25.

write_actions.name: create_campaign
write_actions.risk: creates a new A/B testing campaign visible to the workspace; external mutation, approval required

write_actions.name: update_campaign
write_actions.risk: updates an existing campaign's configuration (name, status, traffic allocation, etc.); can start/pause/stop a live experiment; external mutation, approval required

risk.read: external VWO API read of experiment/campaign metadata
risk.write: external mutation of VWO campaign configuration, including starting/pausing/stopping live A/B experiments; approval required
risk.approval: read: none, read-only campaign directory sync. write: required for all mutating actions (create/update campaigns).

name: waiteraid

base_url.description: WaiterAid API base URL. Pass B correction: the real, currently-documented WaiterAid API is served from app.waiteraid.com/wa-api/<method> (POST-method, query-string-parameterized endpoints), not api.waiteraid.com/<resource> (a REST-shaped host/path this bundle previously modeled but the real API does not expose -- see docs.md).

auth_hash.description: WaiterAid auth hash (obtained once via the real API's own /wa-api/auth?username=&password=&restaurant= endpoint -- this bundle expects a pre-obtained hash, matching legacy's config contract, not username/password directly). Pass B correction: sent as the real API's own 'auth_hash' QUERY parameter on every request, not the X-Auth-Hash header this bundle previously (and legacy) sent -- the real WaiterAid API has no documented header-based auth of any kind, only query-string auth_hash (or username/password, which this bundle does not collect).

restid.description: WaiterAid restaurant ID (a plain numeric identifier, NOT a credential -- reclassified from x-secret in this Pass B revision since it is not credential-shaped; see docs.md). Pass B correction: sent as the real API's own 'restid' QUERY parameter on every request (mandatory on every documented endpoint), not the X-Restaurant-ID header this bundle previously (and legacy) sent.

start_date.description: Optional date filter (YYYY-MM-DD), sent as the real getBooking/searchBooking endpoint's own 'date' query parameter when configured. Renamed in intent from legacy's 'start_date' (config-shape backward compatible: the property name is unchanged) since the real API's own parameter is a single exact-match date filter named 'date', not a lower-bound range filter -- see docs.md.

query.description: Location query (city name, coordinates, IP, or zip) forwarded as the query parameter on every stream's request. Also used to derive the synthetic id field's suffix, matching legacy's fallback id.

historical_date.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) forwarded as the historical_date query parameter on the historical stream.

longitude.description: Longitude forwarded as the marine stream's longitude query parameter. Required for the marine stream only.

autocomplete_query.description: Location text forwarded as the autocomplete stream's query parameter (partial city/region/zip/IP text for typeahead matching). Required for the autocomplete stream only; independent of the query key every weather-data stream uses.

scraping_job_ids.description: Comma-, whitespace-, or semicolon-separated Web Scraper Cloud scraping job IDs to fan out over for the problematic_urls stream (one request per id). Required for that stream only.

write_actions.name: create_sitemap
write_actions.risk: creates a new sitemap (scraper configuration) in the caller's Web Scraper Cloud account; low-risk, does not itself start scraping any site

write_actions.name: update_sitemap
write_actions.risk: overwrites an existing sitemap's start URLs and selector configuration; any scraping job created from this sitemap after the update uses the new configuration

write_actions.name: delete_sitemap
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a sitemap; any scraping job history tied to it is not itself deleted but the configuration can no longer be reused or edited

write_actions.name: create_scraping_job
write_actions.risk: starts a real scraping run against the sitemap's (or start_urls override's) target site(s); consumes page credits from the caller's Web Scraper Cloud account for every page scraped

write_actions.name: delete_scraping_job
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a scraping job and its scraped data; any already-downloaded export is unaffected, but the job's stored records become unrecoverable through the API

risk.read: external Web Scraper Cloud API read of the caller's own sitemap/scraping-job/account/problematic-URL metadata
risk.write: external mutation of the caller's own sitemaps and scraping jobs; create_scraping_job starts a real scraping run against a target site and consumes page credits from the caller's account, and delete_sitemap/delete_scraping_job are irreversible through the API
risk.approval: required for create_scraping_job (consumes billable page credits and issues real outbound requests to a third-party site) and for delete_sitemap/delete_scraping_job (irreversible); create_sitemap/update_sitemap are low-risk (configuration only, no outbound scraping)

name: webflow
description: Reads Webflow sites, collections, collection items, pages, forms, form submissions, assets, asset folders, webhooks, redirects, custom domains, components, orders, products, and ecommerce settings, and writes CMS collection-item lifecycle actions, form-submission hidden-field updates, asset metadata, webhook subscriptions, and ecommerce order/inventory mutations, using the Webflow Data API v2.

api_key.description: Webflow API token (Site or OAuth access token). Used only for Bearer auth (Authorization: Bearer <api_key>); never logged.

site_id.description: The Webflow site ID to read collections, pages, and forms from. Required by every stream (legacy's siteResource helper fails without it).

base_url.description: Webflow API base URL override for tests or proxies.

accept_version.description: Optional Webflow Data API version to send as the Accept-Version header (e.g. 1.0.0 or 2.0.0). Omitted entirely when unset.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

write_actions.name: create_collection_item
write_actions.risk: creates a new staged (unpublished-to-live) CMS item in the given collection; consumes the site's CMS item quota; the item is not visible on the live site until a subsequent publish_collection_item call

write_actions.name: update_collection_item
write_actions.risk: overwrites staged field data on an existing CMS item (primary locale only, unless cmsLocaleId is set); changes are not visible on the live site until a subsequent publish_collection_item call

write_actions.name: delete_collection_item
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a staged CMS item from the collection; if the item was previously published live, it remains live until a subsequent unpublish, since delete only affects the staged copy per Webflow's staged/live item model

write_actions.name: publish_collection_item
write_actions.risk: publishes the current staged content of the named item ids live immediately, making them visible on the site's live domain(s); does not itself trigger a full site publish/build

write_actions.name: update_form_submission
write_actions.risk: overwrites the values of hidden fields already defined on the form's schema for one submission; cannot add new fields or edit visible/user-submitted answers

write_actions.name: update_asset
write_actions.risk: renames or re-captions an existing site asset (display name / alt text only); does not replace the underlying file

write_actions.name: delete_asset
write_actions.risk: permanently deletes an uploaded asset from the site's asset library; any live page still referencing the asset's URL will show a broken image/file link

write_actions.name: create_webhook
write_actions.risk: registers a new outbound webhook subscription for the site (up to 75 per triggerType); Webflow will begin POSTing event payloads to the given url immediately for matching events

write_actions.name: delete_webhook
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a webhook subscription; Webflow stops sending event payloads for it immediately

write_actions.name: update_order
write_actions.risk: updates internal order record-keeping fields (comment/shipping provider/tracking number/tracking URL) on a live ecommerce order; does not change order status or trigger customer notifications by itself

write_actions.name: fulfill_order
write_actions.risk: marks a real customer order as fulfilled and, unless sendOrderFulfilledEmail is explicitly set false, sends the customer a fulfillment notification email

write_actions.name: refund_order
write_actions.risk: DESTRUCTIVE FINANCIAL ACTION: reverses the underlying Stripe charge and refunds the customer's payment in full, setting the order's status to refunded; cannot be undone through the API

write_actions.name: update_inventory
write_actions.risk: changes live storefront stock levels for a SKU either absolutely (quantity) or incrementally (updateQuantity); an incorrect value can oversell or wrongly zero-out a product's live availability

risk.read: external Webflow API read of site collections, pages, forms, assets, webhooks, redirects, ecommerce orders/products, and CMS collection items for a configured site
risk.write: external mutations against a live Webflow site: CMS collection-item create/update/delete/publish, form-submission hidden-field updates, asset rename/delete, webhook subscribe/unsubscribe, and ecommerce order fulfillment/refund/inventory changes; publish/fulfill/refund actions have customer- or site-visitor-visible side effects and refund is irreversible
risk.approval: required for all write actions; refund_order and publish_collection_item are high-risk (irreversible financial action / immediate live-site visibility) and should be gated more strictly than the others

month.description: YYYY-MM-01 month identifier (or the 'current' alias) required by the 'months' stream's per-month detail path; also accepted by scheduled-transaction reads' since_date-equivalent narrowing is not applicable here (months has no since_date param).

write_actions.name: create_transaction

Body is wrapped under a top-level "transaction" key (YNAB's own POST /budgets/{budget_id}/transactions convention) — the record itself carries that wrapper, since the engine's write dialect sends record fields verbatim as the JSON body with no nested-wrapper construction primitive (see teamwork/bitly precedent).

write_actions.name: create_category
write_actions.risk: external mutation; creates a new budget category within a category group; approval required

write_actions.name: update_category
write_actions.risk: external mutation; renames/re-notes/re-goals an existing budget category; approval required

write_actions.name: delete_scheduled_transaction

name: zendesk-sunshine
description: Reads and writes Zendesk Sunshine legacy custom object types, objects, relationship types, and relationships.

base_url.description: Your Zendesk Sunshine API base URL (e.g. https://yoursubdomain.zendesk.com/api/sunshine). No derived default: must be provided explicitly (see docs.md Known limits).

email.description: Zendesk agent email address, combined with api_token for HTTP Basic auth as '{email}/token'.

api_token.description: Zendesk API token, used as the Basic auth password alongside '{email}/token' as the username.

object_type.description: Optional legacy object type key to filter the objects stream (sent as the ?type= query param). Zendesk's Legacy Object Records endpoint requires at least one filter parameter; omitting this returns every type-unfiltered record the account exposes to an unfiltered request, matching legacy's own unfiltered call -- but the real API 400s if the account has no default-filterable view, see docs.md Known limits.

relationship_type.description: Optional legacy relationship type key to filter the relationships stream (sent as the ?type= query param). Same 400-without-a-filter caveat as object_type, see docs.md Known limits.

write_actions.name: create_object_record
write_actions.risk: creates a new record of an EXISTING legacy object type; low-risk external mutation, no approval required. Legacy custom object TYPE creation is blocked by Zendesk as of January 15, 2026, but creating records of already-existing types remains supported until the full legacy API sunset (July 27, 2026)

write_actions.name: upsert_object_record_by_external_id
write_actions.risk: creates a new record with the given external_id if none exists, or overwrites the attributes object of the existing record with that external_id and type -- an overwrite, not a merge: any attribute omitted from this call's attributes is cleared on an existing record

write_actions.name: delete_object_record
write_actions.risk: permanently deletes a legacy object record; Zendesk requires every relationship record referencing this object record to be deleted first, or this request fails

write_actions.name: delete_object_type
write_actions.risk: permanently deletes a legacy object type definition; only succeeds if every object record of that type has already been deleted. Standard Zendesk object types (users, tickets, organizations) cannot be deleted this way and the API rejects the request

write_actions.name: create_relationship_record
write_actions.risk: links two existing object records (legacy custom object records, or a mix of custom and standard Zendesk records) via an EXISTING relationship type; low-risk external mutation. Legacy relationship TYPE creation is blocked by Zendesk as of January 15, 2026, but creating relationship records of already-existing types remains supported until the full legacy API sunset (July 27, 2026)

write_actions.name: delete_relationship_record
write_actions.risk: permanently removes a relationship record between two object records; irreversible, does not affect either underlying record

write_actions.name: delete_relationship_type
write_actions.risk: permanently deletes a legacy relationship type; only succeeds if every relationship record of that type has already been deleted

risk.read: external Zendesk account read of legacy custom object types, objects, relationship types, and relationships
risk.write: external mutation: creates/upserts/deletes object records of existing legacy object types, creates/deletes relationship records between them, and deletes object/relationship type definitions. Zendesk blocked creating new legacy object/relationship TYPES as of January 15, 2026, and will fully remove the legacy custom objects API on July 27, 2026 -- this bundle's write surface is scoped to what remains supported today
risk.approval: required for all write actions; read access uses a read-only Basic-auth API token with no approval needed

name: zendesk-support

name: zoho-analytics-metadata-api
description: Reads Zoho Analytics workspace/view/table/organization/folder/query-table/datasource metadata and triggers datasource/view data syncs, via the Zoho OAuth 2.0 refresh-token grant.

spec.title: Zoho Analytics Metadata API Connection Specification

client_id.description: Zoho OAuth 2.0 client ID for the refresh-token grant. Used only in the token-request form; never logged.

client_secret.description: Zoho OAuth 2.0 client secret. Used only in the token-request form; never logged.

refresh_token.description: Long-lived Zoho OAuth 2.0 refresh token. Exchanged for a short-lived access token at token_url; never logged. The 3-legged consent/acquisition dance is out of scope (credentials layer already owns it).

base_url.description: Zoho Analytics Metadata API base URL override for tests or region-specific data centers (e.g. https://analyticsapi.zoho.eu/restapi/v2).

token_url.description: Zoho OAuth 2.0 token endpoint override. MUST be https in production; the hook fails closed on a non-https or unparseable value to prevent exfiltrating the refresh token to an attacker-chosen endpoint.

org_id.description: Optional Zoho Analytics organization ID; sent as the ZANALYTICS-ORGID header on every request when set.

workspace_id.description: Zoho Analytics workspace ID required by the folders/query_tables/datasources streams and the sync_datasource/refetch_view_data write actions, all of which are workspace-scoped paths in the real Metadata API (unlike the flat legacy-parity workspaces/views/tables streams). Reading/writing those without this set fails with an unresolved-config-key error naming workspace_id; every other stream/action does not require it.

mode.description: Runtime mode: live (default) or fixture for credential-free conformance.

write_actions.name: sync_datasource
write_actions.risk: triggers an asynchronous data sync for one datasource in a workspace; low-risk (re-fetches data from the connected source, does not itself mutate any Zoho Analytics record). The documented optional CONFIG query parameter, which can carry a datasource's own username/password credential for the sync, is NOT supported by this action (see docs.md Known limits) -- only the no-CONFIG invocation shown in Zoho's own sample request is modeled

write_actions.name: refetch_view_data
write_actions.risk: triggers an asynchronous data refetch for one view from its available datasource; low-risk (re-fetches, does not itself mutate any Zoho Analytics record). Same CONFIG-credential limitation as sync_datasource -- see docs.md Known limits

risk.read: external Zoho Analytics API read of workspace/view/table metadata plus organizations, recently-accessed views, shared workspaces/dashboards, folders, query tables, and datasources
risk.write: triggers an asynchronous datasource or view data sync/refetch in Zoho Analytics; does not create, modify, or delete any Zoho Analytics workspace/view/table/data record itself -- only re-pulls from an already-configured external datasource
risk.approval: required for write actions (sync_datasource/refetch_view_data); read access uses the same OAuth refresh-token grant with no separate approval

location_id.description: Location ID or external ID used by the location_details stream and optional log filtering.

user_id.description: User ID used by the user_details stream.

device_stats_start_date.description: Start date/time for device uptime and response stats, in the format expected by Zonka Feedback.

device_stats_end_date.description: End date/time for device uptime and response stats, in the format expected by Zonka Feedback.

distribution_logs_start_date.description: Start date for distribution logs in YYYY-MM-DD format.
